data.MSHP_TaskLogDesc: Weekly Call

Completed the agreed Request Tracking Dashboard enhancements following the client review. Queue selection was updated so the Request Workitems table now displays only the current active workitems associated with the selected queue or task, aligning the displayed records with the queue counts.

Queue visibility was also enhanced to respect the logged-in user’s task and group assignment permissions, while keeping the full authorized Queue Management list visible when a specific queue is selected. The Read-only Preview was restricted appropriately for non-admin users, the Comments tab was removed, and Modified Data tracking was improved to better capture user-entered changes by task or workflow stage.

The corresponding frontend and backend scripts were updated, packaged, and shared with the client for deployment and environment testing. The development is completed and ready for client validation.

Enhanced the overall performance of the Request Tracking Dashboard by optimizing the data-loading flow and improving the efficiency of the supporting backend logic. The work focused on reducing loading times, improving responsiveness, and ensuring the dashboard handles data retrieval more effectively. The group-based visibility logic was also refined so records are filtered correctly according to each user’s assigned groups. These updates improved both dashboard performance and the accuracy of the information displayed to different user groups. The enhancements were applied and are ready for further validation.

Participated in a detailed review session with Ecobank focused on the Request Tracking Dashboard, particularly Queue Management behavior, workitem visibility, role-based access, Modified Data tracking, and dashboard tab usage.

The session clarified that queue cards and the Request Workitems table should reflect the same current active-task context, with queue visibility restricted according to the logged-in user’s task and group permissions. Additional decisions were confirmed around restricting Read-only Preview access, removing the Comments tab, and improving Modified Data so it better represents user-entered changes by workflow stage. The agreed requirements and implementation priorities were captured for development.

MSHP_AllActiveProjWithTasks.MSHP_ExecutiveSummary: Enhanced el panel de seguimiento de solicitudes: se mejoró el flujo de datos, la lógica backend y el rendimiento para optimizar la carga de datos, la capacidad de respuesta y la precisión del filtrado de registros según los grupos de usuarios. Estas actualizaciones mejoran el rendimiento del panel y la precisión de los datos, alineando los registros mostrados con los recuentos de colas. Se refinó el comportamiento de gestión de colas: se desarrollaron, revisaron e implementaron mejoras para alinear la visibilidad de las colas y los elementos de trabajo activos según las tareas de usuario y los permisos del grupo. Se restringió el acceso de vista previa de solo lectura, se eliminó la pestaña de comentarios y se mejoró la precisión de los datos modificados para capturar los cambios introducidos por el usuario en una etapa de flujo de trabajo para una mejor representación. Sesión de revisión detallada: participación en una revisión enfocada con Ecobank sobre el panel de seguimiento de solicitudes, aclarando los requisitos y decisiones relacionados con la gestión de colas, el acceso basado en roles, la visibilidad de elementos de trabajo y el uso de pestañas del panel. Se capturaron requisitos y prioridades acordados para el desarrollo, asegurando la alineación con las necesidades y expectativas del cliente.

Completed a second independent review of the Collateral Release Process to challenge and validate the findings from the initial assessment and ensure no important implementation detail or enhancement opportunity had been overlooked. The review revisited the full process structure, routing, assignments, screens, scripts, notifications, error handling, reporting, and operational behavior with a stronger focus on identifying design weaknesses, edge cases, and opportunities to simplify or improve the target solution.

The second pass also reassessed the previously proposed recommendations to determine whether they remain the best implementation approach or whether a more maintainable, resilient, and scalable design can be introduced. Additional attention was given to approval sequencing, resubmission behavior, segregation of duties, exception handling, escalation paths, automation reliability, reporting, auditability, and opportunities to reduce unnecessary workflow complexity.

The expanded assessment provides a more comprehensive and implementation-ready view of the current process and the potential redesign, with the objective of presenting the client with stronger enhancement options and clearer priorities for the next phase.

data.MSHP_TaskLogDesc: Weekly Calls

Completed the fix for the Offboarding UAT issue affecting contractor details in the email subject line. The problem was isolated to the subject and case-title mapping, while the email body was already correctly handling employee and contractor information dynamically.

A normalized Parting Person Name variable was added to the form-data normalization script so the same value can be used consistently for both Stonnington employees and contractors. The related name, email, and job-title mappings were also aligned to ensure the correct person information is available throughout the process.

The fix was implemented and validated in both Dev and Test environments, and the contractor name is now displayed correctly in the email subject and related process data.

Completed the Resignation Letter development and validated the full workflow end to end. The process now prepares the required acknowledgement-letter data, dynamically populates the approved template with the employee and resignation details, generates the final document, and sends it to the employee as an email attachment.

The workflow was updated to include the acknowledgement-letter data preparation step before document generation, followed by the Generate Letter task and the Send Letter to Employee email task. The routing logic was also preserved so acknowledgement letters are generated only for Resignation and Retirement cases, while Dismissal and Cancel paths bypass the letter generation.

The complete flow has been tested successfully, including data mapping, document generation, conditional routing, and email attachment delivery.
Welcome dashboard first draft mock-up and development.

data.MSHP_Project: Banco de Tierra del Fuego - Managed Services 2.0

data.MSHP_TaskLogDesc:
Completed the deployment and end-to-end validation of the global date-format automation in both DEV and TEST environments. The process was configured to enforce the standard d&#x2F;m&#x2F;Y H:i format automatically and is now scheduled to run daily at 11:00 PM, ensuring that new or modified user profiles remain aligned with the required configuration.

Testing confirmed that the automation correctly identifies users requiring updates, applies the new format, verifies the result after the API update, and records execution metrics and exceptions. Users with incomplete mandatory profile information, such as missing email, first name, or last name, are identified separately without preventing the remaining users from being processed successfully.

The DEV and TEST configurations are completed and validated. The next step is to coordinate the corresponding migration, configuration, and validation in Production following the agreed deployment protocol.
